claims.text: The stage-3 refund saga keeps Đơn Hàng's own data consistent (order, refund row in donhang_payments, email) but never compares those rows with what Gateway A actually did; goal 2 of refund-requirements.md needs that comparison.
Reconciliation compares two independent records of the same money, Payments' refund rows and the gateway's report, and explains every line on which they differ.
The gateway's report is Gateway A's refund history, exportable as CSV at any time through its admin page and its API (criterion T7); in the lab GET /v1/refunds on fake-gateway stands in for it.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/reconciliation-requirements.md @ stage-4 lines 18-20; docs/team/payment-gateway-evaluation.md T7 rows

claims.text: Scope: only refunds through Gateway A, including hand refunds on its admin page (ĐS-2); charging out (Payments has no charging flow); refunds outside the gateway out: bank-transfer orders (ADR 0010) and refusals handled by customer care (R4).

claims.text: refund-requirements.md left open what list accounting needs and how often; reconciliation-requirements.md answers: one run a day, results before the next working morning (assumed, accounting confirms); refund-requirements.md is not edited.

Scenarios: ĐS-1 gateway refunded but row failed (answer lost), within a day; ĐS-2 gateway refund with no row (e.g. by hand on admin page), within a day; ĐS-3 refunded row missing from report, after one more run, within two days; ĐS-4 amounts differ, within a day.
Every difference is explained by staff; none disappears by itself.
Estimate: 1% of orders ask for a refund (assumed), about 500 a normal day, about 1,000 on the busiest; one daily run compares about 1,000 lines a side, a small batch; load does not shape the design.

Assumptions and confirmers: the report carries each refund's idempotency key refund-<row id>, like the lab's GET /v1/refunds, which pairs a line with its row (gateway developer); once a day is enough (accounting); a refund near day end may appear only in the next day's report (gateway developer).
Ranked drivers: (1) every difference explained; (2) each difference found within a day; (3) only people correct money rows, no job corrects them itself.
Before refunds were built, customers called customer care and staff refunded by hand on the gateway's admin page and told accounting by email.
RefundSender sends the key refund- plus the row's id on every call for one row; a gateway refusal marks the row failed with the reason and the saga compensates the order from refunding back to paid.

claims.text: ADR 0010's exit plan step 3 exports Gateway A's refund history as CSV and keeps it with backups, so accounting can still reconcile after the contract ends.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0010-cong-thanh-toan-ben-ngoai.md @ stage-4 Kế hoạch rời đi, step 3

claims.text: Trading off: checking nothing never finds ĐS-1/ĐS-2; checking after each refund sees differences sooner but costs a call per refund and still misses hand refunds with no row; a daily run is a small batch at the price of differences unseen up to a day (two for ĐS-3).

Keeping correction with people (driver 3) makes every change to money a decision someone made, at the price of staff time per difference; a self-correcting job would close differences sooner with nobody accountable.

Choices: an hourly demand from accounting changes the scenario measures before the design; a report without the idempotency key is a risk to settle in the test environment, since pairing a line with a row needs some key; the near-midnight case is why ĐS-3 waits one more run.

The key refund-<id> stops one row being refunded twice but not a refund with no row (ĐS-2); RefundSender marks a row failed on a refusal or once GiveUpAfter (24 h) has passed since the request with no answer, though the gateway may have refunded (ĐS-1).
claims.source_hint: DonHang.Payments/RefundSender.cs @ stage-4 RecordResult, RefundSettings.GiveUpAfter; fake-gateway/Program.cs answers by Idempotency-Key

claims.text: A timeout ends the wait, not the work, so a call with no answer says nothing about whether the gateway refunded.
Payments sets a refund row to refunded from a single Refunded outcome of the gateway call.
